newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ROMARIO REJOINS FLAMENGO AFTER LESS THAN THREE MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMARIO REJOINS FLAMENGO AFTER LESS THAN THREE MONTHS.

text.p: Brazil's World Cup striker Romario rejoined Flamengo on Friday after less than three months with Spanish club Valencia.
The two clubs agreed terms on Friday to the relief of the striker, who has fallen out with Valencia coach Luis Aragones, and ended a transfer saga that had dragged on for nearly two weeks.

Sources at Flamengo, where Romario spent 18 months before leaving for Valencia, said he had been signed on loan for until July of next year but they were unable to give further details of the transaction.
Romario will team up with Bebeto at Flamengo to renew the partnership that provided eight goals on the way to Brazil's triumph at the 1994 World Cup.
Romario, who appeared at a news conference wearing a Flamengo shirt, said: "With Bebeto, I will try and provide Flamengo with the thing they need most which is goals."

Valencia sources had said on Wednesday that the deal, which began with Flamengo president Kleber Leite travelling to Valencia the week before, was definitely on, only to announce on Thursday that it was unlikely to take place.
Negotiations continued Friday with Valencia directors arriving in Rio and holding an all-day meeting with their Flamengo counterparts.
Valencia had been interested in an exchange deal involving 22-year-old winger Savio, the club's biggest revelation for years, a proposal which Flamengo resisted.
Flamengo said their Argentine midfielder Alejandro Mancuso, who appeared during Friday's negotiations, was not involved in the deal.
Romario spent 21 of his 78 days at Valencia in Rio and was twice dropped by Aragones, on the second occasion for oversleeping and arriving late for training.
Despite the fuss over his return, he is only likely to a handful of games before the end-of-season break.

Flamengo have only seven games left in the first stage of the Brazilian championship and look unlikely to make the quarter-finals. Their hopes of winning the South American Supercup were extinguished when they lost to Chile's Colo Colo.

Flamengo boast the biggest support of any Brazilian team but their form in the Brazilian championship has been wretched with four defeats in their last five games, three of them by a scoreline of 4-1.
Many doubt whether Romario's return will be enough to end their woes.
Critics say what Flamengo really need are a stronger defence, a more creative midfield and a change in the ultra- cautious tactics they say are employed by coach Joel Santana.
Romario's relationship with Bebeto, despite the fruits borne in the last World Cup, has not always been sweetness and light.
The two have entirely different personalities and at one stage in their careers fell out altogether, trading insults in the media.
